rubric_notes: Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 2.08 lineage, all four curated families with SCCS and protein-level members, homology implied at superfamily/family but not fold/class, all supported by the bundle; automated-match bins correctly described as placement buckets. States superfamily-level homology and keeps core histones in the closer family, but the function-transfer caveat is attached only to fold/class levels; it never explicitly says that shared a.22.1 superfamily membership itself does not justify transferring nucleosome or chromatin function to TAF, bacterial, or archaeal domains, so the third must_include item is met only implicitly.

Correct domain and family SUNIDs (113676/116993, 122676/140797), shared superfamily a.204.1 SUNID 101386, all supported by bundle. States probable common ancestry at superfamily strength, separate families, and rejects transferring HisE histidine-biosynthesis role or MazG substrate specificity without independent evidence. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family SCCS, superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55 and class c, with the bundle's homology endpoint confirming homology implied at the superfamily level as the answer claims. Correctly infers remote common origin and a shared structural framework, and explicitly blocks transfer of HSP70 chaperone behavior, actin polymer biology, and hexose phosphorylation across families, plus quaternary structure, active-site loops and insertions. Regulation not named explicitly but the limits are otherwise complete and correctly scoped; no errors.

Correctly places a.25.1.1/47241, a.25.1.2/47253, a.25.1.3/100951 under superfamily a.25.1/47240 and fold a.25/47239 (all supported by bundle children/homology responses). Frames the relationship as divergent homology rather than fold convergence, distinguishes fold-level from superfamily-level evidence, and explicitly refuses transfer of reaction, metal preference, substrate, quaternary assembly, and catalytic residues without independent sequence/structure/active-site evidence. Correctly separates the a.98/c.7 R1 domains (supported by search results). Does not literally name biochemical assays but the external-evidence requirement is equivalent in substance. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage and all three families with SUNIDs under b.6.1/49503; explicitly notes homology implied at superfamily level and not at fold b.6; rejects copper/electron-transfer transfer from b.6.1 or b.6 membership and requires conserved copper-ligating-site evidence plus independently conserved biochemical function. Facts supported by the children/parents/homology responses in the bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

SCCS, SUNIDs, and lineage verified against the bundle; correctly notes homology is implied at the d.15.1 superfamily but not the d.15 fold, matching the homology endpoints. Infers remote common ancestry and shared beta-grasp core, and rejects using an RBD hit to annotate ubiquitin conjugation or UBX/p97-adaptor function and using a UBX or ubiquitin-like hit to imply Ras binding, requiring family-level or direct evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct families, superfamily (52172), fold, class with supported SUNIDs. States remote superfamily-level lineage and explicitly denies that all CheY-like domains have response-regulator activity. Rejects transfer of two-component phosphorylation/signaling, ODC catalysis, and KaiA clock activity; notes ODC catalytic domains are classified elsewhere (supported by search results showing c.67.1.5 and d.125.1.1), demonstrating domain-recruitment awareness. Does not cite the KaiA annotation, but that is not required. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct lineage with SUNIDs (310706, 310577, 310616), fold comment, all four sibling superfamilies named, homology_implied flag at 310577 cited and verified. States homology restricted to the b.84.5 superfamily/family (V1 and A1 protein nodes), shared b.84 fold does not assert ancestry with siblings, and transfer of function/active-site/template relationships across b.84 would be unsafe without independent evidence. Does not explicitly say the split is not positive nonhomology evidence, but frames correctly as a non-assertion.

Correct 2.08 fold f.21 (81344) and superfamilies f.21.1/81342, f.21.2/81343, f.21.3/103501; correctly cites that homology is implied at each superfamily node but not at the fold (bundle homology endpoints). Keeps function/template transfer within superfamilies and does not claim absolute non-homology. Omits the requirement that cross-superfamily homology would need independent sequence, structural, motif, and biological-context evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct family SCCS/SUNIDs (c.2.1.1/51736, c.2.1.8/51900, c.2.1.9/63944) under superfamily c.2.1/51735, fold c.2, class c, all supported by the children/parents/homology evidence. Reads superfamily as remote common ancestry, distinguishes it from family identity, explicitly rejects transfer of ADH reaction, CoA/succinyl-CoA synthetase role, K-channel regulation, substrate specificity, oligomeric context and catalytic residues, and notes fold membership is not a homology assertion. Minor looseness in 'broad NAD(P)-binding expectation' is immediately qualified by the need for independent ligand evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Domain SUNIDs 98768 and 61142 and the full shared lineage are correct, family SUNID 100905 'not a true family' is cited as the release-specific caveat, and the answer explains that the usual family/superfamily-implies-homology rule is unsafe here while still describing the pair as co-grouped designed trimeric coiled-coils. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 1.69 (d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 in own fold/superfamily/family; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_ c.23.14.1; shared class only) and 2.08 (d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 with SUNIDs 106249/106250, c.23.14.2 under c.23 and c.23.14; 1f8y stays c.23.14.1). Notes l.1.1.1 tag artifacts are not the core domains. Interprets change as new same-superfamily remote-homology relationship, hedges template use as 'plausible remote', and refuses family membership and reaction transfer. Bundle-supported.

Identifies d1a14h2 as the 8-residue H:1-8 segment, sunid 343393, SCCS l.1.1.1 under class l Artifacts with Tags/N-terminal Tags/Synthetic lineage; d1a14h1 as the real mouse VH domain in b.1.1.1. Rejects homology, function transfer, and template use from tag similarity, allowing it only as an artifact flag. Identifiers match bundle; mouse species is correct though not in the cited bundle. Complete. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Complete before/after chain: single d1acca_ SUNID 43828 f.11.1.1 through 2.03, split by 2.04 and still in 2.08, with both SIDs, SUNIDs, boundaries, and full lineages. Draws the multidomain-fusion conclusion, restricts transfer by residue range, and correctly separates family and superfamily homology signal from fold and class.

Correct five-domain inventory, boundaries, SCCS, mosaic interpretation, new fold d.394, and function-transfer caveats. However it asserts that 'the 3jb9A endpoint' reports 3jb9A as its own chain-cluster representative, yet the bundle contains only the five parents responses; that API-dependent claim is unsupported by this answer's evidence (noncentral). Evaluator: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy, domain lengths 51/373/752 supported by sequence endpoints, family repeat record with representative 4cj9 A:259-292 and correct non-projection caveat, correct homology vs fold-level distinction. Does not mention the re heterogeneity annotation on d2kq5a_/d3v6pa_ even though its bundle contains it, so the annotation-interpretation criterion is only partly met.

States 2.08 / 2.08-stable and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16, but its evidence bundle contains only the 2.08 downloads manifest, which carries no latest_periodic_update field, so the periodic label claim attributed to the current-release endpoint is not supported by this answer's evidence. The non-immutable-snapshot note is supported by the downloads notes. Advises citing 2.08-stable but omits preserving the dated label for periodic-only entries, and does not explain that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places d1br0a_, d1ez3a/b/c_, and d1dn1b_ in a.47.2.1 under a.47 STAT-like / a.47.2; cites the three-helical-fragment comment and ms flag, the automated match to d3c98b_, and bundle-supported SEQRES lengths (120/124 vs 222) to show the fragments cover only part of the larger domain. Rejects spectrin homology from fragment resemblance, limits homology to family/superfamily, and recommends complete 1dn1B/3c98B structures as templates. All must_include items met in equivalent wording; no must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Lists five NAD(P)-binding superfamilies across folds c.2, c.3, c.31, c.25 and e.52 spanning classes c and e, all supported by the cited search and parents endpoints; correctly reports the homology endpoint showing c.2.1 implies homology while c.2 carries the above-superfamily warning. Frames NAD(P) binding as a recurrent solution rather than a single ancestor, sets superfamily as the homology boundary, and requires full-domain sequence/structure evidence before transferring specificity, function, or templates. Complete and accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

States the 2.04 separation into different folds and superfamilies and the 2.08 co-placement in b.18.1 with b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 remaining distinct, and cites the superfamily homology scope to justify a remote common-ancestry reading rather than a close relationship. External support is the PubMed 17977833 family annotation naming d1nqdb_, d1w99a3, and d2quoa_, with d1w99a3 correctly placed in the same family as the Cry3A domain and d2quoa_ in b.18.1.37. Notes 1dlc's other domains lie outside b.18.1 and refuses transfer of insecticidal activity, pore formation, or collagen binding. Eval: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 lineage through protein/species nodes; homology justified because the shared node is the family, not the class/fold; hf correctly described as domain-level, different fold from exemplar with similar sequence/SSE count; states the flag does not remove d1ztra1 from the family but makes coordinate-level equivalence unsafe; excludes same-fold positive training use unless heterogeneity is explicitly modeled; function transfer only as a hypothesis needing independent evidence. All cited facts (family homology scope fa, mutant comment) supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy, boundaries, protein branches, and fr semantics with supporting bundle (including sequences). Homology retained; align only present residues, treat absence as missing data, do not score gaps as indels; prefer unflagged complete domain as representative/template and use fragment only for tissue-factor-specific questions; avoids artificial subfamily or inflated diversity; rejects protein-level function transfer. Quality of candidate representatives not discussed but recommendation is hedged. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation and correct hierarchy semantics; globin example (a.1 SUNID 46457, a.1.1 SUNID 46458, a.1.1.1 SUNID 46459) and the homology_implied_by_level fold/superfamily/family statements are all supported by the evidence bundle. Explains that family placement asserts homology plus a closer grouping and that a new fold asserts the domain fits no known fold. Weak on the fourth criterion: does not name the kinds of evidence that would support upgrading to an existing superfamily, so the classification-as-evidence-integrating-hypothesis point is left implicit. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.4 under superfamily d.144.1 (fold d.144, class d), all supported by the bundle. States superfamily-level common ancestry and that fold alone does not imply homology. Explicitly rejects projecting APH aminoglycoside specificity, PI3K lipid specificity, and PIKK/activation-loop regulation across families. Lists sequence/orthology, catalytic and substrate-residue conservation, domain architecture, ligand-bound structures, and biochemical assays as required evidence. No material errors.
